title: Shared decision-making and disease management in advanced cancer and chronic kidney disease using patient-reported outcome dashboards.
production_reason: [E1] PROMIS health-related quality of life measures are outcomes of a clinical dashboard intervention, not the research object.
audit_reason: [RU] The co-designed PRO dashboard is the intervention, but the abstract is ambiguous about whether its evaluation is measurement implementation or only clinical impact.

title: Stated-Preference Survey Design and Testing in Health Applications.
production_reason: [E4] This paper provides general guidance for stated-preference surveys of patient preferences, not health-state valuation or health measurement.
audit_reason: [RU] The paper studies design and testing of stated-preference surveys in health, but the abstract does not specify whether the methods include health-state valuation.

title: Acceptability and perceived barriers to adoption of the core outcome set for maternal and neonatal health research and surveillance during emerging and ongoing epidemic threats (MNH-EPI-COS). An online survey
production_reason: [E4] This survey assesses adoption barriers for a maternal-neonatal core outcome set, not a health measurement instrument.
audit_reason: [R2] The study evaluates the acceptability, outcome definitions, and data-collection feasibility of a standardized maternal and neonatal core outcome set.

title: Methods for Evaluation of Surrogate Endpoints for HTA Decision Making: A Good Practices Report of an ISPOR Task Force
production_reason: [E4] This task-force report recommends methods for validating surrogate endpoints for HTA, without a direct health-measurement or health-state-valuation focus.
audit_reason: [R2] The task force report develops methods and good practices for validating surrogate health endpoints against patient-relevant outcomes.

title: Did a digital quality of life (QOL) assessment and practice support system in home health care improve the QOL of older adults living with life-limiting conditions and of their family caregivers? A mixed-methods pragmatic randomized controlled trial
production_reason: [E1] Tests whether access to QOL data improves patient and caregiver QOL; QOL assessment is an intervention outcome.
audit_reason: [R2] The digital system for collecting, displaying, and integrating quality-of-life assessment data into home care is the primary intervention under evaluation.

title: Comprehension of and preferences for visualization of patient-reported outcome data to support clinical decision making: A systematic review
production_reason: [E4] Reviews visualization preferences for communicating PROM results in clinical decisions, not evaluation of a health measure.
audit_reason: [R2] The review directly evaluates user comprehension and preferences for visualization formats used to communicate PROM data.
